description: ERUPTION is developing a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer—an interactive learning experience that introduces young learners to space exploration through engaging missions, quizzes, and simulations. Our goal is to make space education accessible and inspire curiosity, teamwork, and problem-solving. We welcome collaborators in development, design, storytelling, and space science.
summary:
Moonbase Mission is an interactive educational game that challenges players to keep four astronauts safe through seven mission rounds on the Moon. Players manage oxygen, water, food, power and crew safety while deciding how to spend limited credits on batteries, water recycling, a greenhouse and radiation shielding.

The game makes engineering trade-offs understandable: producing oxygen consumes water, growing food requires resources, and surviving the lunar night requires stored energy. Players can preview the consequences of their choices before running each round.

Illustrated guides, optional spoken instructions and visual resource indicators support learning. Drawing on NASA resources about life support, lunar technology, radiation protection and growing plants in space, the prototype introduces young learners to mission planning and interconnected systems. Game values are simplified for education and are not NASA measurements.
details: Moonbase Mission: Junior Astronaut Trainer is a browser-based educational game designed to help young learners understand the decisions involved in operating a lunar outpost. HOW IT WORKS Players manage a crew of four through seven mission rounds, balancing oxygen, water, food, power and crew safety. Limited credits can be spent on a battery, water recycler, greenhouse and radiation shelter. Each round, players choose upgrades, distribute power and preview the predicted effects before running their plan. Decisions create connected consequences: oxygen production consumes water, greenhouse growth requires water and electricity, and batteries help the outpost operate during the lunar night. Resource shortages can end the mission early. LEARNING AND CREATIVITY The game turns abstract engineering concepts into practical decisions with visible results. Illustrated guides provide explanations, while crew portraits, resource indicators and optional spoken instructions support the experience. Players learn by planning, observing consequences and trying different strategies. The intended impact is to encourage curiosity about space exploration, resource conservation and systems thinking. Learning outcomes have not yet been formally evaluated. NASA RESOURCES NASA resources covering environmental control and life support, lunar surface technology, radiation protection and growing plants in space informed the educational concepts. The game simplifies these topics into understandable mechanics. Resource quantities, costs and the seven-round timeline are learning models, not NASA measurements or operational mission predictions. TECHNOLOGY AND DEVELOPMENT The prototype uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single web page. SVG illustrations provide character portraits and visual elements. WebGL supports a three-dimensional lunar scene on compatible devices, with a static fallback when unavailable. Optional narration uses the browser’s speech synthesis, so voice availability and quality depend on the device. Claude assisted with code generation and visual implementation. ChatGPT supported planning, review and project documentation. AI assistance is disclosed in the submission. DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS Development priorities included understandable instructions, readable controls, mobile access, limited device resources and clear feedback. Subtitles allow play without sound, and animation and graphics settings provide flexibility. The current version is an educational prototype; its scientific modelling, accessibility and device compatibility can be developed further.
